page: Microsoft Azure D16_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv3 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, the processor supports AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA instruction sets, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU.

For storage, the D16_v3 includes 410 GB of local SSD capacity. Benchmark evaluations reveal clear performance trade-offs. Single-core processing capabilities, such as those measured by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, fall into the bottom 10% tier. Conversely, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores. Memory read bandwidth is average at 54.45 GB/sec for large blocks, whereas large-block write bandwidth is weaker, placing in the bottom 25% at 23.36 GB/sec.

With its balanced resource density, the D16_v3 is suited for general-purpose workloads. It achieves average throughput in static web serving at 8.88 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 9.27 million operations per second. The instance is appropriate for multi-threaded applications, moderate database operations, and standard web serving, but is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or heavy LLM prompt processing.
